rows.grounds: the Lord in the sky of awareness

items.question: What do the satisfied goddesses of consciousness do after consuming the universe?
premises: The goddesses of consciousness are fully satisfied.
Bhairava rests in the full heart as the space of consciousness.
They abide in that deity without any difference.
items.inference: Satisfied consciousness rests non-dually in the heart of Bhairava.
items.plain_english: Satisfied, they rest without difference upon the god Bhairava, who dwells in the space of consciousness within the full heart of their own self.

rows.grounds: due to varied functions, names, and contemplations

items.question: How can manifold forms appear if the goddesses remain non-different?
premises: The goddesses engage in various acts, names, and forms of worship.
Their essential nature remains non-different.
Manifold forms appear within that non-difference.
items.inference: Multiplicity of form arises from functional variation without breaking non-dual unity.
items.plain_english: Thus, through immersion in various acts and the multiplicity of names and worship, their manifold forms appear even within non-difference.

rows.grounds: through invoking and withdrawing the goddesses
in groups increasing from one to nine and beyond

items.question: How are the different groupings of the goddesses formed?
premises: The same goddesses can be invoked or withdrawn.
Their groupings vary in number.
The numbers range from one up to nine and beyond.
items.inference: The numerical classifications of the goddesses arise from their invocation and withdrawal.
items.plain_english: And through the invocation and withdrawal of these very goddesses, they are arranged in groups of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and more.

rows.grounds: the detailed divisions starting with Rudra, the sun, and Kalasena

items.question: Why does the text turn away from detailed enumerations of difference?
premises: The expansion of difference includes systems like Rudra, the sun, and Kalasena.
Further elaboration of these details is unnecessary here.
The discussion must return to the present topic.
items.inference: The text sets aside extensive classifications to focus on the main subject.
items.plain_english: The expansion of difference beginning with Rudra, the sun, and Kalasena is vast; but enough of such detail—now attention is directed to the present topic.

rows.grounds: in the manner of a mirror image

items.question: How does the manifested universe appear within consciousness?
premises: The entire group of manifested beings appears in the self of consciousness.
It appears as a reflection.
One for whom it appears thus is the Lord of the universe.
items.inference: The universe shines as a reflection in consciousness, revealing the Lord of the universe.
items.plain_english: This entire manifested group of beings shines as a reflection in the self of consciousness; he for whom it shines thus is indeed the Lord of the universe.

rows.grounds: who has this kind of thought-free recognition

items.question: Who is considered to be established in the Shambhava means?
premises: A person may have a constant non-conceptual recognitive awareness in the self.
This awareness is always arising.
Such a person is sealed by the Shambhava means.
items.inference: Constant non-conceptual recognition of the self constitutes the Shambhava means.
items.plain_english: One in whom such a non-conceptual recognitive awareness constantly arises within the self is indeed sealed by the Shambhava means.

rows.grounds: practices like mantra, mudra, ritual, and worship

items.question: What practices are required in this supreme Shambhava means?
premises: The recognition of full I-ness has been clearly explained.
Mantra, seal, ritual, and worship are other practices.
None of these other practices apply here.
items.inference: The Shambhava means consists solely in the recognition of full I-ness, not in external practices.
items.plain_english: This recognition of full I-ness has been explained; in this means there are no other practices such as mantra, seal, ritual, or worship.

items.question: What is attained by repeatedly resorting to this non-conceptual immersion?
premises: One repeatedly resorts to non-conceptual immersion.
This immersion leads to the state of Bhairava.
That state is called liberation while living.
items.inference: Repeated non-conceptual immersion results in liberation while living.
items.plain_english: Resorting again and again to this non-conceptual immersion, one attains the state of Bhairava, which is called liberation while living.

rows.grounds: the formulation of means and end even in summary form

items.question: What is the focus of the discussion from this point onward?
premises: The discussion now turns to liberation while living.
This includes a brief formulation of means and goal.
The topic is examined from here onward.
items.inference: The text now investigates liberation while living and its related means and goal.
items.plain_english: From this point onward, liberation while living is examined, including a brief formulation of the means and the goal.

items.question: How can liberation be discussed in the previous pathless state where no difference exists?
premises: In the previous chapter there was not even a conception of difference.
That state was without means.
Where there is no difference or means, the process of liberation cannot be described.
items.inference: Liberation as a process can only be discussed once some framework of means appears.
items.plain_english: But in the previous chapter there was not even any conception of difference; therefore, in that pathless state, who is liberated, how, and from what?

items.question: How should the wise understand the fiftyfold division in relation to the Shambhava means?
premises: The Shambhava means is a non-conceptual recognitive awareness.
A fiftyfold division was indicated earlier.
The wise should apply that division within this awareness.
items.inference: The fiftyfold division is to be understood as integrated within non-conceptual recognition.
items.plain_english: In the non-conceptual recognitive awareness called the Shambhava means, the wise should apply the fiftyfold division that was indicated earlier.

rows.grounds: the earth element through thought-free awareness
beholding reaches the state of Bhairava
this same method applies to water and the rest

items.question: How does non-conceptual recognition apply to the elements like earth?
premises: The earth can be seen as reflected in one's own self.
This seeing occurs without conceptual thought.
The same method applies to water and the other elements.
items.inference: Recognizing each element as a reflection in the self leads to Bhairava-hood.
items.plain_english: Seeing the earth itself reflected in one's own self with non-conceptual awareness, one attains the state of Bhairava; this same method applies to water and the other elements.

items.question: What is the highest principle reached at the end of this contemplative ascent?
premises: The ascent culminates in a supreme principle.
That principle transcends all coverings.
It is all-pervading, independent, all-knowing, and known as Shiva.
items.inference: The final object of contemplation is the supreme, free, and omniscient Shiva.
items.plain_english: Finally, there is the supreme principle beyond all coverings, all-pervading, independent, all-knowing, which is conceived as Shiva.

rows.grounds: even that reflected in the mirror of pure awareness

items.question: What happens when even the supreme Shiva is seen as a reflection in pure consciousness?
premises: Even the supreme principle appears as a reflection in unconstructed consciousness.
One may see this without conceptual thought.
Such seeing leads to becoming Bhairava.
items.inference: Non-conceptual recognition of even Shiva as a reflection reveals one's own Bhairava nature.
items.plain_english: Seeing even that supreme principle reflected in the mirror of unconstructed, vast consciousness, and free of conceptual thought, one spontaneously becomes Bhairava.

rows.grounds: firmly resting in the unified awareness of one object despite its parts

items.question: What analogy illustrates stable non-conceptual awareness of a single object?
premises: One may see a red object in front with non-conceptual awareness.
The awareness remains unified despite various aspects of the object.
This illustrates stable, indivisible perception.
items.inference: Non-conceptual awareness can grasp a single object as an indivisible whole through its varied aspects.
items.plain_english: Just as, seeing something red in front with non-conceptual awareness, one remains firmly established in the indivisible awareness of a single pot through its various aspects...

rows.grounds: likewise from every grouping starting with earth
becoming aware of one's own nature

items.question: What is the result of recognizing one's self through each aggregate of experience?
premises: The analogy of unified perception applies to aggregates beginning with earth.
One recognizes one's own self through them.
The self then shines forth as full.
items.inference: Recognizing the self in every aggregate reveals the fullness of one's own being.
items.plain_english: So too, recognizing one's own self through each aggregate beginning with earth, one shines forth as full and complete.

rows.grounds: this has arisen from me alone

items.question: What three recognitions constitute the Shambhava means?
premises: The universe is recognized as arisen from the self.
The universe is recognized as reflected in the self.
The universe is recognized as non-different from the self.
items.inference: The Shambhava means unfolds through three recognitions: emanation, reflection, and non-difference.
items.plain_english: “This has arisen from me alone, this is reflected in me alone, and this is not different from me”—this threefold recognition is the Shambhava means.

items.question: How does the Spanda teaching summarize creation, maintenance, and withdrawal?
premises: Creation, maintenance, and withdrawal have been briefly indicated.
The Spanda teaching addresses where things abide and from where they arise.
This summary supports the Shambhava recognition.
items.inference: The Spanda teaching concisely grounds the threefold cosmic process in the self.
items.plain_english: This brief indication of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal has been made; as the Spanda teaching states, it concerns where the universe abides and from where it arises.

rows.grounds: and so any other defining mark

items.question: What further characteristic is needed beyond the sovereignty and universality of consciousness?
premises: The supreme sovereignty of consciousness has been revealed.
Its identity as the self of the universe has been revealed.
No further defining characteristic is required.
items.inference: Recognizing consciousness as sovereign and universal is sufficient.
items.plain_english: By this alone the supreme sovereignty of consciousness and its nature as the self of the universe have been revealed; what other characteristic need be stated?

rows.grounds: having the universe as one's nature

items.question: How does the recognition of oneself as creator reveal Bhairava-nature?
premises: The universe is manifested in the space of one's own consciousness.
One recognizes oneself as the creator and universal self.
This recognition unfolds as Bhairava-nature.
items.inference: Recognizing oneself as the creator within consciousness reveals one's Bhairava identity.
items.plain_english: “In my own self, in the space of consciousness, I manifest the universe; I am the creator, the universal self”—through this unfolding recognition, Bhairava-nature is revealed.

rows.grounds: the entire set of sixfold paths
with the recognition that I sustain it
the nature of being the universe

items.question: How does recognizing maintenance in oneself reveal universal form?
premises: The entire sixfold path is reflected in the self.
One recognizes oneself as the maintainer of that reflection.
This recognition makes universal form clear.
items.inference: Seeing oneself as the sustainer of all reflected paths reveals one's universal form.
items.plain_english: “The entire group of the six paths is reflected in me alone; I am the one who maintains it”—through this recognition, one's universal form becomes clear.

rows.grounds: in the self blazing with constant supreme knowledge
with the recognition that this dissolves in me

items.question: What brings peace when the universe is seen dissolving in the self?
premises: The self is ablaze with ever-risen great awareness.
The universe dissolves in that self.
Seeing this dissolution brings tranquility.
items.inference: Recognizing dissolution in the blazing self leads to peace.
items.plain_english: Seeing that the universe melts in me—in the self matted with the flames of ever-risen great awareness—one becomes peaceful.

rows.grounds: of the dream-world of transmigration containing infinite diversity
rejoicing in the recognition that I am Shiva

items.question: How is the self recognized in the act of dissolving the dream of samsara?
premises: Samsara is like a dream-house filled with endless variety.
That dream is burned away.
One recognizes oneself as Shiva, the exulting fire that consumes it.
items.inference: The self is the Shiva-fire that dissolves the dream of samsara.
items.plain_english: “I alone am Shiva, the exulting fire that burns up the dream-house of samsara, filled with endless varied beings.”

rows.grounds: as undivided despite the acts of emanation, persistence, and dissolution
from the level of that reality

items.question: What realization reveals the fourth state beyond creation, maintenance, and dissolution?
premises: The entire world arises manifoldly from the self.
It remains rooted in the self and dissolves in the self.
One who sees the self as partless despite these divisions shines in the fourth state.
items.inference: Seeing the undivided self through creation, maintenance, and dissolution reveals the fourth state.
items.plain_english: The entire world arises from me in many divided forms, yet it is firmly rooted in me and dissolves in me, with nothing beyond. One who thus sees it as partless despite the division into creation, maintenance, and dissolution shines forth in the fourth state.
